authors: E. R. Gardner, P. J. Jones, H. J. de Nordwall
title: Osmotic coefficients of some aqueous sodium chloride solutions at high temperature
experimental_method: Vapour pressures of NaCl solution and of pure water in two platinum-iridium cells with capacitance diaphragm transducers as null indicators, balanced by nitrogen pressure compared with a mercury manometer; solvent vapour pressure by dead-weight piston gauge.
uncertainties_stated: Random error in pressure difference 0.7% up to 150 C, about 0.3% above; standard deviation of points from smooth curves 5e-3 in phi; piston gauge 0.05%; possible systematic errors at m=1 of 0.025%, 1.9% and 0.13% in dp at 150, 200, 250 C (water-in-both-cells test).
quality_remarks: phi values refer to p = p0 (not 1 atm); the authors estimate the conversion to 1 atm would raise phi by ca. 0.3% at 250 C and ignore it. Molality varies from nominal because of solvent evaporation; the resulting correction to phi never exceeds 0.001 and was neglected. Text layer of Table 1 had several broken cells (corrected from image).

not_extracted_tables.reason: osmotic coefficients read from smooth curves (Fig. 3) at round temperatures; derived/smoothed, with extrapolated entries

changes_after_image_check: table 1 row 16 (3.000): phi 1-021 (text layer) -> 1.021; row 17 and others: mid-dots and dashes normalised to full stops
extraction_notes: The PDF is one article (7 pages); the PDF title line lists authors Gardner, Jones and de Nordwall. Printed mid-dot decimals written as full stops. Sanity: phi decreases with T at each molality; p0 increases with T; Delta p increases with T and m; two replicate-like rows at 1.011 (different T) and 2.006/2.010 (different T) are not duplicates. Concentrations 1.0 to 3.0 mol/kg NaCl, 122 to 270 C.
needs_pass2_reason: Text layer needed corrections after the image check (several cells).
